title: A validation figure compares a computed quantity with an exact or published law, and a miss that is shown is evidence too
summary: Pipe flow against the exact parabola, particle migration against the tubular-pinch equilibrium, and secondary-flow intensity against Dean's scaling are four checks of a low-Reynolds-number solver. Read each for what it is compared against, what the pass or miss label says, and what the footnote text adds.

media.alt: Two log-log panels against Dean number from 2 to 260. Left: measured secondary-flow peak velocity from about 0.0007 metres per second at De = 2 to about 2 metres per second at De = 260, following a red dashed De squared line at low De, bending below it, and approaching a purple dashed De to the 1.63 line at high De; three red crosses at the highest De mark runs that did not converge. Right: the ratio of measured to a literature correlation, rising from 1.2 to about 2.5 near De = 20 and falling back to about 1.2.

source.caption: Dean secondary-flow intensity scaling
source.note: These figures carry PASS, FINDING and MISS labels in the images and long footnotes. The page teaches how to read such labelled validation figures with standard laws only (Hagen-Poiseuille, Dean scaling, Segre-Silberberg equilibrium, Dean-vortex transition) and quotes only numbers printed on the figures.

read_the_figure.question: Does the computed quantity follow a known exact result or published scaling over the range studied, and where does it depart from it?
read_the_figure.axes: Pipe flow: x is r/R, y is u/u_max; the grey curve is the exact parabola and blue dots are the computed values at three radii. Tubular pinch: x is radial position r/R from the axis to the wall; black dots are release radii, blue diamonds final radii after one pipe transit, dashed vertical lines are the model's own equilibrium (green, 0.5R) and the literature value (red, 0.6R). Dean intensity: x is Dean number De on a log axis, y on the left is the peak secondary velocity on a log axis, on the right the ratio to a literature correlation. Four-vortex search: x is De, y is the number of outer-wall crossings of a probe line.
look_at: Pipe flow: the three dots lie on the curve; the label reports a maximum relative error of 2.7e-14.
Pinch: arrows run from release radius to final radius; the inner particles move out and the outer ones move in, towards an intermediate radius. None reaches the line within one transit.
Dean: the slope of the blue line on log-log axes, compared with the slopes of the red (2) and purple (1.63) reference lines. The red crosses are runs that did not converge.
Dean ratio panel: the ratio is not 1 anywhere; the shaded band gives the measured range, 1.2 to 2.5.
Four-vortex: the red line stays at 1 for all De, below the dotted line at 3 that the literature signature would reach.
read_the_figure.proves: Pipe flow at machine precision shows the discretisation reproduces a solution it can represent exactly. The pinch figure confirms a mechanism (migration towards an intermediate radius from both sides) but not the literature equilibrium value. The Dean figure confirms the De squared scaling at low De and shows the departure at high De. The four-vortex figure records a feature that the model did not produce.
if_wrong: Pipe-flow error well above round-off for a profile in the discrete space: boundary condition or mapping error.
Particles all moving to the wall or all to the axis: the lift model has the wrong sign or no balance.
Dean slope that stays at 2 at high De when the literature slope falls: the nonlinearity is not resolved, or the runs did not converge.
A transition that the literature predicts and the model never shows: a limitation of the formulation, a resolution issue or a genuinely different regime.
must_check: Reference law, source and range of validity are named.
Unconverged runs are marked and not hidden (here they are marked with red crosses).
The fit range for each slope is stated.
The quantity compared is the same in model and reference (here the panel plots the ratio).
Residence time or transit length is stated when a trend, not an endpoint, is the evidence.
as_drawn: Pipe flow: dots at r/R of 0, 0.5 and 0.9 with u/u_max of 1, 0.75 and 0.19, which equal 1 - (r/R)^2 exactly: 1, 0.75, 0.19. Label: maximum relative error 2.7e-14.

Pinch: release radii about 0.1, 0.3 and 0.75 (two particles from the outer release radius). Final radii about 0.19, 0.38, 0.64 and 0.70. Model equilibrium line at 0.5R, literature at 0.6R. The footnote says no particle fully equilibrated in one transit.

Dean: the blue line goes from about 7e-4 m/s at De = 2 to about 0.017 at De = 10 (slope about 2), and from about 0.48 at De = 95 to about 0.8 at De = 150, a local slope near 1.1, which is the exponent the orange label gives (1.99 to 1.10). Three crosses at De of about 190, 237 and 260 are unconverged (iteration cap).
Four-vortex: the crossing count is 1 at every De from 2 to 260. A footnote says a perturbed restart at De = 150 returned to the same state to 2e-16 relative.

terms.meaning: Steady laminar flow in a long circular pipe driven by a pressure gradient; the velocity profile is a parabola.
Neutrally buoyant particles in pipe flow at moderate Reynolds number migrate across streamlines to an annulus at about 0.6 of the pipe radius from the axis.
Dimensionless group for curved-channel flow combining Reynolds number and curvature; it sets the strength of the secondary flow.
Circulation in the cross-section of a curved channel, superimposed on the main flow.
The slope of a log-log plot: y proportional to x to the power n gives slope n.
A nonlinear solve whose residual met its tolerance before the iteration cap.

remember: A comparison with an exact solution is the strongest check: error near round-off means the discrete problem is solved exactly.
Local slope on log-log axes is the exponent; a changing slope means a changing regime.
Unconverged points should be shown differently, not dropped and not blended in.
A mechanism check (direction of migration) and a quantitative check (the equilibrium value) are two different claims.
A negative result is only informative if the search was shown to be adequate.

understand.title: Four levels of check
understand.text: The pipe flow checks the flow solve against an exact profile. The pinch figure checks a particle-fluid mechanism qualitatively. The Dean figure checks a scaling law and the shape of its departure. The four-vortex figure checks whether a bifurcation appears. Each is weaker or stronger as evidence: an exact match is strongest, scaling next, a mechanism next, and an absent feature is a limitation.

understand.title: Reading a local slope
understand.text: Between two points on a log-log curve the exponent is the ratio of log changes. In the Dean panel it is close to 2 at low De, where the secondary flow is weak and the Dean perturbation theory applies, and falls at larger De as the secondary flow starts to change the primary flow.

understand.title: What a miss teaches
understand.text: The footnote reports a perturbed-restart search that relaxed to the same state. That converts 'not found' into 'not found where it was looked for', and shows the model has a unique steady state in this range. The reader is then told what to conclude: a limitation of the current formulation, not a missing search.

steps.title: Hagen-Poiseuille profile
steps.note: From the axisymmetric Stokes equation for a pressure gradient G. The three points in the figure at 0, 0.5 and 0.9 give 1, 0.75 and 0.19.

steps.title: Why error can reach round-off
steps.note: If the finite-element velocity space contains quadratics, as many Stokes-stable elements do, the exact parabola is representable and the computed profile equals it to solver round-off. This is why 2.7e-14 is expected, not remarkable; the element used is not stated in the figure.

steps.title: Log-log slope
steps.note: The exponent between two points. In the Dean panel, between De of 2 and 10 with y of 7e-4 and 0.017, it is ln(24)/ln(5), which is about 2.

steps.title: Dean scaling at low De
steps.note: Dean's 1928 perturbation result. The secondary-flow velocity is driven by the centrifugal term, which is quadratic in the primary velocity.

steps.title: Dean number
steps.note: Re is the Reynolds number of the primary flow, D_h the hydraulic diameter and R_c the radius of curvature. Curvature enters only through the square root.

steps.title: Direction of tubular-pinch migration
steps.note: The lateral force changes sign at the equilibrium radius, so particles from both sides converge on it. The figure's arrows show exactly this sign pattern; the position of the zero is the quantity that differs from the literature value.

worked.title: Local slope between two points of the Dean curve
worked.problem: Read from the figure: the measured peak secondary velocity is about 0.48 m/s at De = 95 and about 0.8 m/s at De = 150. What exponent is that, and how does it compare with 2 and 1.63?
worked.answer: About 1.1, below both reference exponents: consistent with the figure's own label (1.99 to 1.10). The project caption's wording, declining toward 1.63, does not describe the plotted high-De slope, which falls below it.

analyze.q: The ratio panel peaks at about 2.5 near De = 20 and falls to 1.2. What does a ratio that is not constant say about the literature correlation as a description of this model?
analyze.hint: The correlation has a different exponent range.

analyze.q: Why is the unconverged-point marking important to the exponent drop at high De?
analyze.hint: The last three points lie on the purple line; are they reliable?

analyze.q: In the pinch figure the two particles released at the outer radius end at different radii. What does that say about equilibration in one transit?
analyze.hint: Final position depends on residence time.

evaluate.q: The model equilibrium is 0.5R and the literature is 0.6R. Is the mechanism confirmed? Is the quantity validated?
Is a miss on the four-vortex transition a reason to withdraw the Dean figure?

create: Design a convergence study for the pinch equilibrium radius: which parameters (mesh length, release radius, transit length) do you vary, and what plot shows the equilibrium is a fixed point?
Draw the Dean intensity plot so that unconverged points, fit range and local-slope values are annotated directly.

checks.q: Why is machine-precision agreement with the Poiseuille profile unsurprising?
checks.hint: What does the discrete space contain?
checks.answer: The exact solution is a quadratic, which the velocity space can represent, so the discrete solution equals it up to solver tolerance.

checks.q: What is u/u_max at r/R = 0.6 in Poiseuille flow?
A log-log slope falls from 2 to 1.1 over the sweep. What does that mean physically?
checks.hint: A change of exponent is a change of regime.
checks.answer: At low De the secondary flow follows the weak-perturbation De squared law; at larger De the secondary flow feeds back on the primary flow and the growth slows.

checks.q: Particles from both sides move towards 0.5R, not 0.6R. What do you report?
checks.answer: That the migration mechanism is reproduced and the equilibrium radius is off by about 0.1R, with the cause (substituted lift coefficients) stated, and no claim of quantitative agreement.

checks.q: What additional evidence would make a null result on a predicted transition convincing?
checks.hint: The search must be shown adequate.
checks.answer: A perturbed-restart or continuation search from several initial states across the range, a refinement study, and a check that the diagnostic would respond if the feature were present.
